Q: Codeigniter: Select from multiple tables A:

CodeIgniter 3's query builder method join() has the following signature.

/**
 * JOIN
 *
 * Generates the JOIN portion of the query
 *
 * @param   string
 * @param   string  the join condition
 * @param   string  the type of join
 * @param   string  whether not to try to escape identifiers
 * @return  CI_DB_query_builder
 */
public function join($table, $cond, $type = '', $escape = NULL)

The $type parameter will be unconditionally converted to uppercase. If $type is a non-empty string, it must be one of the following whitelisted keywords.

  • LEFT
  • RIGHT
  • OUTER
  • INNER
  • LEFT OUTER
  • RIGHT OUTER

As for your script, SELECTing all columns from all included tables is the default setting. If joined tables share identically named columns, you will need to specifically reference the table that particular columns come from and give a differentiating alias for the result set.

get_where() can be used to consolidate from(), where(), and `get() calls.

join() can receive a single column name as the $cond parameter. This means that the tables being joined share an identical column name and there is no column name conflict or ambiguity with other included tables.

Let's join other_table on shared user_id columns.

$default = $this->db
    ->join('other_table ot', 'user_id')
    ->get_where('user_profiles up', ['user_id' => $id])
    ->row_array();

$this->CI->validation->set_default_value($default);

This will render ($id = 34):

SELECT *
FROM `user_profiles` `up`
JOIN `other_table` `ot` USING (`user_id`)
WHERE `user_id` = 34

Q: Email Claim is always missing in the startup.auth.cs but it present in the Token A:

First, you might want to go with direct namespace chaking instead of using EndsWith:

var email = identity.Claims
    .FirstOrDefault(c => 
        c.Type == "preferred_username" || 
        c.Type == "email" || 
        c.Type == "name")
    ?.Value;

You might also want to try using actual CLaimTypes constants:

ClaimTypes.Email or ClaimTypes.Name in your logic:

var email = identity.Claims
    .FirstOrDefault(c => 
        c.Type == ClaimTypes.Name|| 
        c.Type == ClaimTypes.Upn || 
        c.Type == CLaimTypes.Email)
    ?.Value;

This second change should make sure that, if you were running into issues with OWIN's claim remapping, your constants will have the correct translated value.

OWIN will remap your claim names to its own CLaimTypes:

Original Remapped
preferred_username http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/name
email http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/emailaddress
upn http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/upn

Q: OpenCV : How to clear Image Background of ID Card without losing quality A:

Using Rembg to get perfect output like below

Rembg is an offline tool to remove images background. you can simply install Rembg package using pip in python

pip install rembg

afterthat,

rembg i path/to/input.png path/to/output.png

Q: iOS : Testflight No build available for external testers A:

If, like me, you have already submitted your build for beta review and it is approved, and re-adding your tester or group to the build does not fix the problem, try this:

where the build says Approved, click on Notify Testers.

this advances the build status from

[yellow tick] Approved

to

[green tick] Testing

and makes the build available to those external testers.

It is mentioned in the Apple App Store Connect docs here:

If you didn’t select “Automatically notify testers” when you added your build to your group, you must manually notify testers once your build is approved.

...

The build status changes to Testing.

Q: Why to use separate CSS files for components in React.js A:

Yes, you want separate files. No, the reason why you do it isn't for performance (although it certainly can have an impact on performance).

You're missing that components should be re-usable.

If I create an AwesomeWidget component and I want to drop it straight into another project I'm working on then I should be able to do that with as little friction as possible. And you can't do that if its styles are mixed in with application-specific stuff. Your components should be, insofar as is possible, independent of what's around them.

Keep the component-specific files separate and let Webpack do the work of wiring it all up for you. If you find yourself reusing a component enough then move it into its own repo (don't forget you can npm install from a git url if you don't want to publish it to the public package registry).
